Subject: Infra tilt & unit economics: QBR action grid

Team —

Ahead of the QBR next Tuesday I want a concise action grid that ties capacity asks to unit-econ impacts. I outlined a proposed set of asks in the attached spreadsheet but want your updates before leadership sync Friday. High-level goals:

- Show 3 scenarios (Conservative / Base / Aggressive) for GPU slots and expected utilization by week.
- For each scenario, estimate per-inference token cost and a simple sensitivity to batching and KV-prefix caching.
- Call out 2 quick experiments we can run this quarter (slot reshuffle + cache TTL tuning) and expected upside / risk.

Please populate the attachment (qbr-action-grid.xlsx) in the tabs that match your area: Karthik = utilization & slot plans; Ethan = cost math and batching/caching assumptions; Marissa = ops risks and rollout constraints.

Deliverable: updated spreadsheet + short email summary by EOD Thursday (10/15). I'll consolidate for Friday leadership run-through.

Thanks —
Lauren

Subject: Re: Infra tilt & unit economics: QBR action grid

Lauren — thanks, I'm on it. Quick summary of what I'll put into the spreadsheet (draft estimates below) so we can iterate: 

- Base scenario (current): 240 GPU slots across Dedicated + Hosted pool; avg utilization 48%; effective token cost ~$0.0038/token (compute-only) assuming current batching mix.
- Aggressive: +40 slots (burst), util to ~62% but requires burst budget; projected compute token cost down to ~$0.0029/token if batching improvements hit 15% more tokens per request.
- Conservative: hold at 240 slots, enable more aggressive KV-prefix caching (expected ~8-12% token reduction for chat-heavy workloads).

Immediate experiments I propose: 1) Dynamic slot reshuffle (move 20% idle capacity from low-priority models to high-throughput routes for 2 weeks), 2) Batch-size tuning on the 2 highest-throughput routes (increase target batch size, measure latency p95).

I'll attach a short note with the cost math and a CSV snapshot of utilization. Karthik — I left placeholders where I need actual per-pool GPU-hour costs and reserved vs preemptible splits.

Ethan
Senior Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Ethan / Lauren —

Dropped my utilization snapshot into the sheet and added a short assumptions tab. Key notes:

- Raw capacity: 240 total active slots today (175 Dedicated, 65 Hosted burstable).
- Effective utilization calculation: we only count slots that served >=1 req/min sustained over 3h windows; current effective util ~46.8% (close to your 48% estimate).
- GPU cost breakout: Reserved (75%) -> $1.10/GPU-hour; Spot/preemptible (25%) -> $0.35/GPU-hour (weighted blended compute-only cost: $0.91/hr).
- Token math: using our measured tokens-per-invocation distribution (median 70 tokens, 95th 560) I get compute-only token cost of $0.00385 under current batching (avg 1.9 invocations/batch across routes).

Questions / asks for Ethan:
- Can you confirm whether we should include storage egress and networking overheads in the per-token number for QBR (I assume no — keep compute-only and call out other costs separately).
- For the dynamic reshuffle experiment: what policy will re-home capacity? (by route priority or by predicted latency delta?)

I attached a CSV with the per-pool hourly utilization snapshot.

Karthik

Redwood Inference

On Sun, Oct 11, 2026 at 11:40 AM Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Lauren — thanks, I'm on it. Quick summary of what I'll put into the spreadsheet (draft estimates below) so we can iterate: 
> 
> - Base scenario (current): 240 GPU slots...
> - Aggressive: +40 slots...

Ethan / team — ops callouts: 

- Risk: reshuffling slots at scale can cause cold-cache spikes on large-parameter models (we've seen 10-15% latency p95 regressions when hosts are moved mid-session). Need a gradual migration plan with KV warmup prefetching where possible.
- Rollout constraint: Dedicated pool SLA prevents some aggressive reassignments during business hours for enterprise customers (esp. EU customers). We'll need to run reshuffle during the 02:00-06:00 PST window for any move that touches dedicated-reserved capacity.
- Safety net: automatic fallback policy to pin previous mapping for 30 minutes if p95 increases >15% for any route.

I'll add these as a column in the spreadsheet under 'Operational Constraints'. Also recommend we prebook a short 15-minute dry-run window Tuesday morning with the SRE on-call to rehearse the script.

Marissa
Head of Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
